The state implementation readiness gap is the primary near-term OBBB risk surface — state Medicaid agencies had limited advance notice of the final text finalized through the 218-214 House vote, and major states with complex Medicaid populations (Oregon approximately 1.4 million enrollees; Washington approximately 2.2 million) are in early-stage preparation. SALT deduction cap modification, top individual income tax rate reduction (retroactive to January 1, 2026), border security supplemental appropriations release, and energy production incentives are simultaneously effective. Washington state's new 2026 legislative session laws also took effect at midnight — tax provisions, expanded benefits, rural data center guidelines, and healthcare licensing changes — adding to the July 1 simultaneous implementation load. FERC large-load show-cause orders advance to Day 15; AI data center pathway explanation deadline at T-15 (~July 18) — final two weeks of the response window. Amazon Washington State WARN (2,198 positions; 30,000 total corporate layoffs since October 2025) and Bungie/Sony Bellevue (292 layoffs) continue as the structural PNW tech-labor bifurcation backdrop.

The second heat wave will intensify Tucannon's fuel dryness environment and extend Red Flag conditions into the July 4 weekend, four days from now, when human ignition risk (fireworks, holiday activity) overlays the meteorological fire environment. The Winthrop/Okanogan incident is the East Cascades onset period's second geographic suppression front — resource commitment is now split between two active East Cascades fires as the primary July-September risk window opens. Tule Road (Toppenish/Yakima County, approximately 24,087 acres) is approaching full containment, releasing resources for Tucannon. Juniper Dunes (Grant County) near-containment. The Garred Road Fire (approximately 500 acres, 0% containment as of June 30 evening) is monitored as a potential additional ignition. NIFC Preparedness Level 3 advances to Day 15. BPA grid stable. items.summary: Wednesday July 1 opens with the Supreme Court's opinion window for remaining term decisions — the VRA case is among the highest-stakes pending opinions for the November 2026 midterm electoral map. The Court typically releases opinions at 10 AM Eastern (7 AM Pacific); this brief is released pre-ruling. An adverse ruling would enable states to immediately pursue congressional redistricting exploitation — a downstream velocity already demonstrated by Watson v. RNC: states moved on Watson's mail ballot ruling within hours of the June 29 announcement. If the VRA ruling narrows the Act's protections, states under active Republican legislative control with redistricting maps drawn near VRA constraints would be positioned to redraw immediately. The combined Watson (mail ballot grace periods eliminated) plus Trump mail EO (further restriction, TRO requests pending federal circuit) plus potential VRA adverse ruling would constitute a three-track pre-midterm electoral disruption — the most consequential simultaneous disruption since Dobbs (2022). Watson v. RNC Day 3 cascade: Oregon Secretary of State Tobias Read and voting rights organizations have filed TRO requests in federal circuit courts to block the Trump mail-in voting Executive Order. No TRO has been issued as of the morning brief. The OBBB took legal effect at midnight July 1. Medicaid work requirements and per-capita block grant conversion are operative; state implementation readiness gap is the primary near-term domestic risk surface. CMS guidance on enforcement grace periods or waiver application frameworks is the primary resolution mechanism awaited by state agencies. Washington state's new 2026 legislative session laws took effect at midnight. Humphrey's Executor overturned ruling (June 30) enters Day 2 — the 90-year independent agency precedent reversal (FTC, NLRB, SEC) begins its implementation phase, with enforcement priority and independence implications under the current administration. Acting DNI Day 42 — eighth week; the Wednesday morning assessment demand is the highest of the brief cycle: SCOTUS VRA pending, Hormuz Day 13 opening, Lebanon overnight stability, dual IRGC-Hezbollah cyber posture — all requiring integrated IC assessment without confirmed Senate-confirmed leadership.

items.summary: The Pacific Northwest opens Wednesday July 1 morning with compounding wildfire, heat, seismic, and infrastructure developments converging simultaneously. The Tucannon Fire has grown to an estimated 20,000+ overnight acres — continuing advance from 15,000 acres at June 29 evening, driven by record-setting 100-hour fuel dryness for this calendar date (Northwest Coordination Center), persistent Red Flag conditions in southeastern Washington, and limited air attack effectiveness. Level 3 evacuation orders remained active overnight in Garfield County's Pomeroy area. The second PNW heat wave of summer is arriving Wednesday — less than 10 days after the first, with AccuWeather projecting record-challenging temperatures in Seattle and Portland; NOAA's July outlook confirms above-normal temperatures and sustained drought throughout the month. The second heat wave arrives on a fuel environment already described as record-setting by fire behavior analysts; it will extend Red Flag conditions into the July 4 weekend four days from now, when human ignition risk from fireworks and holiday activity compounds the meteorological fire environment. An overnight ignition near Winthrop in Okanogan County prompted full-town evacuation before early-morning partial stabilization — a partial positive, but the fire remains active and constitutes the onset period's second geographic suppression commitment. Oregon coast: an M5.5 earthquake struck approximately 4:35 AM Monday under the Pacific Ocean near the Oregon coast. No significant damage or tsunami warnings were reported. The event is the brief's recurring Cascadia Subduction Zone seismic hazard reminder — the structural long-horizon risk backdrop. A landslide has closed all lanes of Historic Columbia River Highway east of Corbett, according to ODOT — an active transportation infrastructure disruption in the Columbia River Gorge. Elephants Delicatessen in Northwest Portland was destroyed by fire with an arson arrest reported. Lake Chelan (Chelan County) is closed to boaters following a significant influx of logs, ash, and sediment washed in from the 2024 Pioneer Fire burn scar — a secondary disaster pattern disrupting the lake's summer recreational economy at peak season. Fireworks safety concerns across the PNW are elevated heading into July 4 given the compound fuel dryness and heat environment. Tule Road approaching containment, releasing resources. NIFC PL3 Day 15. BPA grid stable. NSF Newport OR operational.

Oregon and Washington face the OBBB's most exposed state conditions: Oregon with approximately 1.4 million Medicaid enrollees and Washington with approximately 2.2 million are among the states with the most complex Medicaid populations under the new work requirement and per-capita block grant conversion. Neither Oregon Health Authority nor Washington State Health Care Authority has issued comprehensive work requirement documentation as of the morning brief. RNC and the Trump mail-in voting EO, managing two simultaneous electoral administration challenges — with the VRA ruling pending this morning as a potential third track. Oregon's election-by-mail system (operative since 2000) requires comprehensive revision of ballot receipt deadlines, voter notification systems, and drop-box infrastructure within five months. Oregon renewable energy construction deadline Friday July 4: Wednesday and Thursday are the last effective business days before the 30-50% federal tax credit qualification window closes. Oregon Governor Kotek's EO 25-25 siting acceleration has enabled project mobilization. Washington Governor Ferguson's SB 6355 (Washington Electric Transmission Authority) is now operative. Portland General Electric's completed acquisition of 140,000 PacifiCorp Washington customers (~$1.9 billion) reshapes the northwest Washington utility map. Columbia River streamflow remains at approximately 340,000 cfs — 54% of historical normal — Drought Year 4 entering July. Washington drought emergency Day 29: fourth consecutive year, 12 emergency counties. Oregon 83% of state in drought. Super El Niño watch: 25% probability (base El Niño approximately 61%); ENSO monitoring update expected this month — a potential fifth consecutive critically dry, warm PNW winter if confirmed. L-Pod orca calf advances to Week 7+ alive. FIFA World Cup PNW venues continue through July 7 with Sound Transit record ridership. PNW residential construction market: permits down across Oregon and Washington as of the latest data. Amazon WA WARN (2,198 positions) and Bungie/Sony Bellevue (292 layoffs) continue as the structural PNW tech-labor bifurcation backdrop. Delta Park BottleDrop Redemption Center (North Portland) closing July 31.

RNC — which produced within-hours gerrymander proceedings following the June 29 announcement.
